research_rationale: Captured Wikisource revision 1670320 contains the full apparent order body: introductory prescription and 13 numbered Panama Canal accounting regulations, signed Woodrow Wilson and dated 4 February 1915. The frozen sole-clause envelope is navigation text; corrected held-text spans are in clauses.csv. Duties recur monthly, semiannually and annually, and include independent bond, inspection, certification and administrative-regulation commands. The packet supplies no source establishing first cessation, formal revocation, or a continuing legal predicate through 2026-10-14. A NO ledger status and silence of numbered-citation searches do not establish a whole-lifecycle end.
savings_reason: Accrued accounting, collection, bond, refund and audit consequences could survive any future termination; no ending instrument or savings provision is held to distinguish them.

earlier_end_check: No own sunset appears in the 13 regulations. Monthly, semiannual and annual deadlines repeat and do not prove final performance or cessation. The packet has no dated first-ending event; the 1937-onward OFR search cannot rule out earlier changes.
scope_check: The single frozen scope is wrong. The captured HTML has 13 numbered regulations; the first held-text span includes the introductory prescription, and the remaining spans separately preserve each numbered rule. Any future end requires clause-specific scope and effective-date analysis.
independent_command_check: Independent recurring commands govern Collector monthly accounts and bond; supporting schedules and papers; Auditor statements and certification; semiannual inspection and reports; account forwarding; crediting/deposit; annual profit transfer; transaction certificates; and Governor administrative regulations. No held source shows a common cessation date.
savings_check: No termination or savings source is in the packet. Past collections, deposits, accounts, bonds, and reports may have accrued consequences, but none proves continuing command or first cessation.
